messages.content: how to get detailed information for an interface?

function.name: requests_get
function.description: Sends an HTTP GET request to retrieve Device Connector Versions information from a specified URL. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

url.description: The URL to which the GET request is sent. The URL points to a JSON file containing Device Connector Versions information.

params.description: Optional query parameters to include in the GET request as key-value pairs.

message.content:
Below are several ways you can pull detailed information about a network interface on a Linux host. Pick the one that best fits your environment (CLI, scripting, or monitoring). | Tool | Typical command | What it shows | When to use | |------|-----------------|---------------|-------------| | **`ip`** | `ip -details link show dev `
`ip -details address show dev `
`ip -details route show dev ` | Full link state, MAC, MTU, flags, speed, duplex, driver, firmware, link‑layer stats, IP addresses, routes, neighbor table | Modern systems; scriptable; replaces older `ifconfig` | | **`ethtool`** | `ethtool -i `
`ethtool -S ` | Driver name, firmware version, supported/advertised speeds, duplex, autoneg, statistics counters (rx/tx errors, collisions, etc.) | Need driver/firmware details or raw stats | | **`ifconfig`** | `ifconfig -a` | Interface flags, MAC, MTU, IP, broadcast, netmask, RX/TX packets, errors, drops | Legacy systems; quick check | | **`nmcli`** | `nmcli device show ` | NetworkManager state, IP, DNS, MAC, driver, firmware, link speed, carrier | Systems using NetworkManager | | **`lshw`** | `lshw -class network -short` | Hardware description, vendor, product, bus info, driver, firmware, configuration | Detailed hardware inventory | | **`sysfs`** | `cat /sys/class/net//speed`
`cat /sys/class/net//duplex` | Raw sysfs attributes (speed, duplex, carrier, link) | Low‑level checks or custom scripts | | **`netstat`** | `netstat -i` | Interface counters (rx/tx packets, errors, drops) | Quick overview of traffic stats | ### Example: Using `ip` for full detail ```bash # Show all link attributes (flags, MAC, MTU, speed, driver) ip -details link show dev eth0 # Show all IP addresses assigned to the interface ip -details address show dev eth0 # Show all routes that use this interface ip -details route show dev eth0 ``` ### Example: Using `ethtool` for driver & stats ```bash # Driver & firmware info ethtool -i eth0 # Statistics counters ethtool -S eth0 ``` ### Example: Using `nmcli` (NetworkManager) ```bash nmcli device show eth0 ``` ### Example: Using `lshw` for hardware inventory ```bash sudo lshw -class network -short ``` --- #### Quick Script Snippet (Bash) ```bash #!/usr/bin/env bash IFACE=${1:-eth0} echo "=== Link info ===" ip -details link show dev $IFACE echo echo "=== Address info ===" ip -details address show dev $IFACE echo echo "=== Route info ===" ip -details route show dev $IFACE echo echo "=== Driver info ===" ethtool -i $IFACE ``` Run with `./script.sh eth0`. Feel free to adapt the commands to your preferred shell or automation framework.
